direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is literally Microsoft Teams the Movie, with the whole movie being a screen recording of a video call of Ice Cube reacting to what is going on, with the production design literally being a Zoom background; The world building is so bad because the animation sequences were probably animated by the dude who made Howard the Alien; The direction on a microscale is nonexistent because it is just actors acting into a Zoom Call Void with no direction or script; The storytelling is genuinely hilarious because the story is so stupid and it is so funny how this movie even got greenlit; They build tension so poorly and so campily that it makes the movie fun bad

performance.comments: Bro is doing the bare minimum from his bedroom because he is clearly acting on Zoom with a green screen on, and is acting to no one; This performance is so over-the-top and so Ice Cube-like that it was actually entertaining to watch how bad it was
Straight up acting to no one on a Zoom call
Most generic evil government employee you can find
Rodrick, what are you doing in this movie?; Actually, it's somewhat enjoyable; Bro went from Diary of a Wimpy Kid to Oppenheimer to this

cast.comments: It's a very tight cast, but it's hard to act with your castmates when you are recording your lines separately via Zoom

story.comments: The concept is Microsoft Teams the Movie; this is straight up a screen recording of a Zoom call for 90 minutes, with the action sequences being a reaction video to the 2005 movie, but they could not get the rights to the movie so they animated the sequences with the dude who made Howard the Alien; the plot structure is so linear and simple that it is funny, the sad part is there is barely any plot so this movie feels incredibly bloated; character writing is just the most templated generic character tropes that it is borderline funny

screenplay.comments: The dialogue feels like it was written the day of the shoot, or just bad improv; The humor is unintentional as it's incredibly funny to see and wonder how this movie was made; I would love to be a fly on the wall for both the behind the scenes for this shoot and the meeting between the filmmaker and the studio when they turned this movie in; The symbolism is just a shallow, generic message of how the government is spying on everyone and how the government is against the people; The foreshadowing is too easy to spot because this movie refuses to take any chances

soundtrack.comments: Straight up, a Spotify playlist, I wish I were kidding

cinematography.comments: Straight up, a screen recording of a Microsoft Teams call; it's super clear this movie was shot in the pandemic, but you can't release this five years after the fact and have us not clown on you for making this movie

editing.comments: Please stop zooming into the screen, it is incredibly nauseating and just bad editing

visual_effects.comments: The CGI for this movie was probably animated by the dude who made Howard the Alien; The CGI for this movie reminds me of those cinematic YouTubers from the early 2010s; The shake effects are like the Disaster ride from Universal Studios (RIP)

review.pacing: Pacing is incredibly slow despite its short runtime, because nothing really happens and every plot point is stretched out
review.climax: Climax and conflict resolution is literally a giant ad for Amazon Prime; The plot resolution makes this movie have no stakes
review.tone: Tone is bad movie camp because there is no way this movie got greenlit, shot, edited, and distributed to the public; The tone for this movie is literally a bad Covid movie as this was clearly shot during the pandemic
review.final_notes: They screencasted the whole movie, but it still looks fake, like it's the real logos, but fake apps; there's no way this dude had WhatsApp on his DHS work laptop
review.overall: Overall, "Microsoft Teams: the Movie" because they basically just screencast Ice Cube's Laptop from his house during the pandemic, as he creates a reaction video to Spielberg's War of the Worlds; but, since they couldn't get the rights to the actual film, they just reanimated it with the dude who made the "Howard The Alien" meme; it's such a bad movie that it's genuinely worth watching just to imagine the meeting that took place when the filmmaker turned his cut into the studio
